thread:
lee: Quick summary from today's cobalt12b quant sweep. Ran int6 (q6/kernel) vs int8 on a mixed RAG + rerank workload. High level: int6 saves ~31% token cost, p95 latency slightly better (~9ms), but rerank MRR@10 drops 2.7% on noisy queries.
ana: can you share the exact slices and traffic assumptions?
lee: slices: retrieval-aug (50%), rerank-short (30%, avg output 40 tokens), long-query-extract (20%, >700 tokens). Traffic sim: 70/20/10 actually. Benchmarked on dedicated n1-gpu pool with 4xA100 equivalent.
yusuf: numbers please (p50/p95/throughput + metrics).
lee: p50: int6 62ms vs int8 69ms (rerank-short). p95: int6 138ms vs int8 147ms. tokens/s: int6 ~1.18x. rerank MRR@10: baseline int8 0.431, int6 0.419 (delta -2.7%). retrieval-aug recall@20: baseline 0.824 vs int6 0.816 (-0.97%). long-query recall suffers most on OCR-noise subset: -4.8%.
rachel: is the MRR drop user-visible? which percentile of users affected?
lee: it's concentrated in low-signal queries (~12% of traffic). For high-confidence queries (click-rate > 0.6) delta is ~0.6% — negligible.
nana: ops stability? any quant-specific failures? memory/latency spikes?
lee: ran 72h soak. No crashes. Observed KV cache pressure for >2k token contexts; had to reduce prefetch batch. One latency jitter incident tied to a background GC in the runtime — fixed by bumping thread-pool.
yusuf: product ask: risk for GTN rerank use-case?
rachel: GTN is sensitive to MRR, we need <1% regression. This looks risky unless we route.
lee: hybrid plan proposed: route retrieval-aug and rerank-short to cobalt12b-int6, route long-query-extract to cobalt12b-int8, with a safety fallback to titan16b-int8 for noisy/low-confidence queries. Sample policy: ```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"max_tokens": 64, "model": "cobalt12b-int6"},
    {"min_tokens": 65, "max_tokens": 400, "model": "cobalt12b-int6"},
    {"min_tokens": 401, "model": "cobalt12b-int8"}
  ],
  "confidence_fallback": {"threshold": 0.35, "fallback_model": "titan16b-int8"},
  "canary": {"pct": 3, "duration_hours": 48, "gates": ["mrr@10_delta","p95_latency"]}
}
```
nana: add cost guardrails: set soft quota for titan spend and alert on >20% of pilot budget. Also need evict policy for long prompts if OOM risk detected.
yusuf: gating criteria suggestion: mrr@10 delta <= 0.8% for GTN rerank slice, recall@20 delta <= 1.5% for retrieval-aug, p95 latency change <= 12ms, cost per million tokens reduction >= 25% (net).
lee: projection: if hybrid stable, platform token-unit-cost drops ~26% given current traffic mix; infra savings after accounting for titan tail are ~18%.
rachel: recommend a conservative pilot: 3% canary for 48h, with focused monitoring on the low-signal subset and automatic rollback on mrr>0.8% breach.
lee: infra notes: will add trace-id injection and evaluation sink for flagged requests. will tag sample queries and store preds for offline QA.
nana: infra-bot can schedule the canary window. infra-bot: scheduled canary deploy for cobalt12b-int6 hybrid -> 2025-09-10T02:00Z, canary 3% for 48h. health endpoints: /serving/health, /eval/sink.
infra-bot: canary alerts: will post to #eng-oncall and create temporary billing cap at 25% over baseline for titan16b.
yusuf: ok, decision: proceed with constrained hybrid pilot. lee to own eval dashboard and tagset, rachel to own product gating thresholds, ana to own deploy automation.
lee: I'll drop the detailed one-pager and a small PR with routing rules into the repo. Closing thread.
